title: What Are the Serbian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget

Culture, not politics: no commentary on regional conflicts or disputed borders. Serbian customs kept in Serbia and the diaspora, including Australia. Leave out virginity or 'proof' customs.

Likely customs (brief finalises): prosidba and the engagement; the kum and kuma; the barjak (wedding flag); the groom's party collecting the bride and buying the bride; shooting the apple (gađanje jabuke) described lightly and safely as often told, no gun detail beyond a source; the Serbian Orthodox service (rings, crowning, common cup, walking around the table); the welcome at the groom's home (bread, a child on the bride's lap) as often told; the kolo with UNESCO 'Kolo, traditional folk dance' (Serbia, 2017) only as far as its text goes; music. Serbian terms with diacritics as sources give them.

Destination angle: Smartraveller Serbia checked live, including higher-level areas; suggest only places outside them, without political framing. Legal from official sources only: the Australian Embassy in Belgrade (CNI, notarial services), Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (recognition), Serbian civil registry steps only if an official page can be read; otherwise 'check with the registry and the embassy, including any fees'; 'as at November 2026'. Serbian-Australian weddings at home through Serbian Orthodox parishes ('ask your parish priest').

Sources: Serbian Orthodox Church official pages (including the Diocese of Australia and New Zealand), UNESCO, Serbia's culture ministry and tourism site, the Ethnographic Museum in Belgrade, encyclopaedias, academic sources. Unsourced becomes 'often told' with no meanings as fact and no [[VERIFY]] marker. One honest framing line per section.
